say: You snap at your colleague and decide they're an idiot, when really it's three in the afternoon and your lunch was a coffee.
Your body was built to handle hunger, but push it too far and hunger can come out as anger.
In one study, sixty-four adults rated their hunger and mood five times a day for three weeks, and the hungrier they were, the angrier and more irritable they felt.
In a lab test, hungry students blamed for a computer crash saw the researcher as harsher, unless they first stopped to think about their feelings.
So eat proper meals at regular times, keep a real snack for late lunches, and before you send that email, ask yourself: am I angry, or just hungry?
Hunger explains it. It doesn't excuse it.
If you take insulin or other diabetes medicines and feel shaky, sweaty or confused, that may be low blood sugar, so treat it straight away, as your diabetes team showed you.
And if you don't have diabetes but get shaky, sweaty or confused when hungry, or you're struggling to cope with stress, see a doctor.
Let's get you back to factory settings.

nhshypo: NHS, Low blood sugar (hypoglycaemia) (last reviewed 3 August 2023, opened 3 Oct 2026): "Low blood sugar usually affects people with diabetes who take insulin or some other diabetes medicines. It's rare in people without diabetes."; symptoms include "feeling hungry", "feeling anxious or irritable", "sweating", "shaking" and confusion; treat it by eating or drinking "something that will raise your blood sugar quickly" and checking again after 10 to 15 minutes; See a GP if: "you do not have diabetes and you get symptoms of low blood sugar such as shaking, sweating, a fast heartbeat and feeling confused"
nhsstress: NHS, Stress (reviewed 6 Mar 2026): behavioural signs include "being irritable and snappy"; "See a GP if: you're struggling to cope with stress; things you're trying yourself are not helping"
maccormack2018: MacCormack JK, Lindquist KA. Feeling hangry? When hunger is conceptualized as emotion. Emotion, online 11 June 2018 (findings read in the University of North Carolina release on Neuroscience News, re-opened 3 Oct 2026; the paper itself was not opened): over 200 university students, fasting or fed; a tedious computer task programmed to crash, then a researcher blamed the student; hungry participants who were not focused on their emotions saw the researcher as "more judgmental or harsh"; "Participants who spent time thinking about their emotions, even when hungry, did not report these shifts in emotions or social perceptions."
whostress: WHO, Stress (questions and answers, 30 March 2026, re-opened 3 Oct 2026): "Try to eat a balanced diet and to eat at regular intervals."; "If we have difficulties coping with stress, we should seek help from a trusted health-care provider or from another trusted person in our community."
swami2022: Swami V, Hochstöger S, Kargl E, Stieger S. Hangry in the field: An experience sampling study on the impact of hunger on anger, irritability, and affect. PLOS ONE 2022;17(7):e0269629 (re-opened 3 Oct 2026): "Sixty-four participants from Central Europe completed a 21-day experience sampling phase", five time points a day, "9,142 responses"; "Greater levels of self-reported hunger were associated with greater feelings of anger and irritability, and with lower pleasure."; effects "remained significant after accounting for participant sex, age, body mass index, dietary behaviours, and trait anger"; limits: single-item measures, situational context not measured
